title: What is getelementptr in LLVM IR, really?

glossary.note: LLVM address arithmetic: base pointer plus scaled indices.

key_points: LLVM IR nests module, function, basic block, instruction.
A block ends with exactly one terminator.
getelementptr only computes an address; load and store touch memory.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Jo is sure about one instruction. She bets lunch on it.

visuals.text: claim: getelementptr reads the array element

beats.speaker: jo
beats.text: GEP fetches the array element. It's in the name: get element.
beats.say: G E P fetches the array element. It's in the name: get element.

beats.speaker: mina
beats.text: Bet accepted. First, how LLVM IR is organized.
beats.say: Bet accepted. First, how L L V M I R is organized.

beats.speaker: mina
beats.text: A module holds functions. A function is a list of basic blocks. A block is a list of instructions.

beats.speaker: mina
beats.text: Every block ends with exactly one terminator, like ret, br or switch. Phi nodes may only open a block, and every value has a type.
beats.say: Every block ends with exactly one terminator, like ret, B R or switch. Phi nodes may only open a block, and every value has a type.

beats.speaker: mina
beats.text: Third line. It takes a base pointer and an index.

beats.speaker: mina
beats.text: It computes p plus i times four. That's all. It touches no memory.

visuals.text: p + i × 4: an address, no memory read

beats.speaker: mina
beats.text: The load, on the next line.

beats.speaker: mina
beats.text: GEP computes where. Load does the access. Splitting them keeps address math optimizable like any other arithmetic.
beats.say: G E P computes where. Load does the access. Splitting them keeps address math optimizable like any other arithmetic.

beats.speaker: mina
beats.text: On arm64, clang folds the pair into one load, with the index shifted left by two.

visuals.text: observed on arm64, output trimmed to the load line

beats.say: On arm sixty-four, clang folds the pair into one load, with the index shifted left by two.
